messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: GPU instability detected in infer-prod-7 (us-west-2). Multiple Xid/driver resets and container restarts reported, elevated 5xx for gpt-large serving. Immediate on-call required. Telemetry: https://telemetry/redwood/infer-prod-7 - Severity: P1

alex: ack, I'm on call. digging in.

maria: i'm pulling pod logs and driver logs now. any immediate customer impact?

customer-ops: CS reporting a handful of customers seeing OOM/503s on embed and chat endpoints, some requests timing out. They want ETA to share.

alex: seeing repeated kernel messages on node infer-prod-7: Xid 31 and 13 spamming, container kubelet restarting gpu driver. ramp in correctable ECC before uncorrectable.

maria: log snippet from /var/log/kern.log:

```
[345672.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, pid=2345, GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU-uuid 
[345672.123789] Out of memory: Killed process 2345 (serve) total-vm:1254320kB, anon-rss:...
[345673.000001] nvidia_uvm: UVM page fault: invalid access at 0x7f8a...
```

lee: confirmed pods on that node are flapping: inference/serve-gpt-large-0  CrashLoopBackOff because driver reset kills process. Other nodes stable.

infra-bot: Runbook: https://wiki/redwood/runbooks/gpu-driver-reset - recommended actions: cordon + drain, preserve KV caches where possible, fallback to lower-memory model.

alex: plan: 1) cordon infer-prod-7, 2) gracefully drain non-critical inference pods with 60s grace, 3) enable fallback routing for high-QPS customers to gpt-medium, 4) open a customer bridge. anyone object?

sasha: +1. prioritize customer-facing routes for fallback. maria, can you confirm which pods have persistent KV that we should not evict?

maria: checking - embedding-cache has persistent volume claim pv-emb-12 on node. we'll try to migrate service by restarting on other nodes first. if migration fails, we will snapshot cache.

alex: executing cordon:

```bash
kubectl cordon infer-prod-7
kubectl drain infer-prod-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 --timeout=10m
```

maria: while draining, I'm tailing driver logs and will attempt safe-driver-reload once pods evacuated. running: `sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200 | grep Xid`

infra-bot: Observability: node gpu temp jumped to 92C before resets; ECC correctable errors increased 4x in last 5m. Suggest physical hardware check if persists.

alex: fallback routing enabled for routes rtx_embed/routing and chat-prod with pin to gpt-medium. policy set to 50% fallback for canary then ramp.

customer-ops: bridge created for impacted customers, join link: https://bridge.redwood/BR-3345678901. CS notified and posting to impacted customers with preliminary ETA 30-45m.

lee: drain finished for non-persistent pods. embedding-cache PV remained; we intentionally left those running to avoid data loss. two pods did not reschedule due to taints on available nodes — raising capacity.

maria: attempted driver soft-reload: `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service` — immediate Xid storm during reload, decided to power-cycle GPU process: `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 0` ; GPU reset completed, I see driver come back without immediate Xid.

alex: after reset, pods on node started recovering but one container had corrupt local state and OOM at restart. evicted that pod and it rescheduled onto infer-prod-3 successfully.

infra-bot: Telemetry update: errors per minute dropped from 320 to 18 in the 12m after reset + fallback. 90th pct latency for chat endpoints returned to baseline.

sasha: customer impact summary for bridge: ~8 customers impacted intermittently, major traffic shifted to fallback so no complete outages. CS posted update.

alex: moving node to maintenance: marking for hardware inspection and creating support ticket with provider. Ticket: PROVIDER-7892.

maria: captured driver core dump and saved diagnostics bundle: /tmp/diag-3345678901.tar.gz (uploaded to S3). Relevant files: kern.log, nvidia-smi -q reports, container logs.

sasha: action items: 1) postmortem to include: cause analysis (ECC -> Xid escalation -> OOM cascades), why fallback didn't trigger earlier (routing policy gap), improve graceful drain defaults; 2) add early detection alert for ECC correctable multipliers; 3) run fleetwide job to verify kernel-driver compat matrix. assigned: alex, maria, lee. timeline: draft in 48h.

alex: thanks everyone. closing this bridge in 30m if stable.

customer-ops: will follow up with customers and escalate if they ask for root cause.

sasha: closing note: marking P1 -> mitigated. will kick off postmortem. :white_check_mark:
